items.content:
To help alleviate server congestion following the release of Patch 8.0, we will be enabling cross-region Data Center Travel between the North American and European data centers during scheduled maintenance on Tuesday, December 1, 2026.

Cross-region Travel Available Beginning Tuesday, December 1, 2026:

  • Japanese data center → Oceanian data center
  • North American data center → European / Oceanian data centers
  • European data center → North American / Oceanian data centers
In the North American and European data centers, login queues tend to become extremely long during peak times following an expansion release, and lengthy wait times may occur immediately after the launch of Patch 8.0. As peak play times differ between North America and Europe, another physical data center may be less crowded and serve as a viable option when login queues on your usual data center are long. While players connecting from geographically distant locations may experience increased latency, we encourage you to try playing on a different physical data center before the expansion launches. As previously announced, cross-region Data Center Travel has until now been restricted to the Oceanian data center due to substantial differences in player population, market economy, and social norms between data centers. However, we have received ongoing feedback from players wishing to travel between the North American and European data centers, and many players in both regions are able to communicate in English even when it is not their first language. Taking these factors into consideration, we have decided to temporarily open travel between these two data centers as part of our efforts to mitigate congestion. We will continue to take community feedback into account as we carefully evaluate the possibility of permanently enabling travel between the North American and European data centers, as well as opening travel between other physical data centers. Learn more about how to use Data Center Travel and its restrictions.

items.title: Review: Final Fantasy XIV Online (Switch 2) - An Expansive Port That Demands Your Commitment
items.content:
Final Fantasy XIV Online has been through quite a rollercoaster journey over the years on its way to becoming one of the most respected MMOs in the industry. Its 2010 launch was a disaster, plagued with performance issues and shoddy design that torpedoed its reputation.

Rather than pulling the plug early, Square decided to swap in a new director to salvage it, leading to a reboot in 2013 called A Realm Reborn. Since then, the game has mostly gone from strength to strength across over a decade of expansions and is now in the process of building up its second major arc.

Though this isn’t the first time Square Enix has brought Final Fantasy XIV to console, it is the first time it’s come to a Nintendo platform, and I’m happy to report that it stuck the landing. The full fat experience is here in all its glory, giving you access to a high quality and addictive RPG experience that’s sure to be in the running for one of the most content-rich games ever produced for a handheld.

The narrative places you in the role of a self-insert character in the land of Eorzea who comes into the picture just as geopolitical tensions are on the rise. After a catastrophic war five years earlier, the expansionist Garlean Empire was repelled by the city-states comprising the Eorzean Alliance, but its leaders desire revenge and are winding up for another grab at ultimate control.

Amid this, you’re also told through a vision by a mysterious goddess of light named Hydaelyn that you’re her chosen champion, and she tasks you with finding six magical crystals to ward off the servants of an approaching darkness.

Thus, we set off on the early steps of what came to be called the Hydaelyn-Zodiark Saga, a four-part fantasy epic that should take you no less than two-hundred hours to complete, and that’s assuming that you beeline for the finale and engage in almost no side content. After all that, there’s then a whole other expansion that’s in the early stages of setting up the next ten-year arc.

Suffice to say, Final Fantasy XIV features one of the richest storylines available in a modern RPG, weaving together the subplots of various nations, factions, and supporting characters to make for an impressively complex and deep narrative.

The downside to this, however, is that the pacing can be all over the place. The 60-hour story of the base game alone is basically an extended exposition dump detailing all the major players in the world and setting the stage for the building conflict to come, meaning you spend a lot of time scrolling through line after line of unvoiced text from NPCs telling you about very interesting story beats that happened some other time offscreen.

This leads to a narrative experience with some incredible highs and disappointing lows. Once the plot picks up steam and starts focusing more on current events, there are lots of awesome character moments and payoffs that make all the time investment up to that point feel worth it. Yet between those moments, it can sometimes feel like the plot really takes its time focusing on largely irrelevant or uninteresting subjects that you simply have to endure to reach the good stuff.

Gameplay design follows the expected structure of an MMO, giving you an enormous living world to explore packed with jobs and levels to grind, side quests to fulfill, minigames to fool around with, dungeons to raid, and a massive story to gradually uncover.

As long as you stick to the Main Story Quest chain, you'll be toured around all the main points of interest in an area and progressively introduced to core mechanics and objectives at a measured pace. Side quest content then fills out the world with more detail and texture, though tons of the quest objectives admittedly boil down to 'bring me three boar skins' fetch quests.

A big part of what makes the gameplay loop so addicting is the versatility of your character, who can independently level dozens of jobs that fill out various combat and non-combat roles. In a combat role, your job is built around a growing variety of cooldown-based actions, echoing the classic Final Fantasy ATB system that blends turn-based and action gameplay.

Every combat job has its own distinct gimmicks and features, such as how the Thaumaturge operates by repeatedly shifting between two passive states that bolster either damage output or MP regeneration. Mechanics like this keep fights from feeling too much like you’re just watching cooldown icons on a hotbar, and there are enough distinguishing traits to make the various classes all feel like they’re worth experimenting with.

Non-combat roles are just as dynamic, even without the pressure of attacking foes. If you're working as a Goldsmith, you can create various bits of armour and jewellery, and it's much more involved than merely clicking the 'Craft' button on a menu after you have the materials.

items.title: Final Fantasy 14 Is Letting Players Travel Between North American And European Servers For The First Time In 16 Years And Fans Are Psyched
items.summary: Mr. Yoshida, tear down this wall
items.content:
Whenever there’s a new Final Fantasy XIV expansion, especially one as hotly anticipated as Evercold is, queues to log into the game infamously become a slog. To combat this inevitable server congestion, Square Enix has announced that it will permit cross-region travel between North American and European data centers.

Starting after the scheduled maintenance on December 1st, players will be able to hop between North American and European data centers at will, or pop over to the Oceanian data centers if they so choose. Here’s the breakdown of the new server traffic flows:

Cross-region Travel Available Beginning Tuesday, December 1, 2026

To help alleviate server congestion following the release of Patch 8.0, we will be enabling cross-region Data Center Travel between the North American and European data centers during scheduled maintenance on Tuesday, December 1, 2026.

— FINAL FANTASY XIV (@en.finalfantasyxiv.com) 2026-11-24T12:00:45.707Z

Square Enix’s reasoning is quite simple; peak player times vary across regions so when the servers are slammed in North America, players can choose a European data center to potentially sidestep thousand-player-deep log-in queues and vice versa. ot only is this a great way to get ahead of the impending server traffic jam, but it’s also a neat social feature that eases some of the siloing that happens between servers.

Currently, if you have a cross-continental friendship, you’d have to make an alternate character on the appropriate data center in order to play together. Cross-region travel will let you port your main character over, letting you quest together and, critically, run endgame content like raids without the need to start from scratch on a new server. That’s huge and players are suitably hyped for it, hoping that the option to data-center-hop remains available permanently.

Square Enix warns that visiting other data centers might increase latency and encourages players to test it out before Evercold launches in February 2027 to get a feel for it. Also, sorry to Oceanian data center players, you still don’t get to go anywhere for now.

items.title: FF14 Free Trial Extended To Lapsed Players Ahead Of Evercold
items.summary: In preparation for Evercold, Square Enix is giving away 30 days of free game time to eligible players and has a new item for purchase that'll let you skip Dawntrail
items.content:
If you are like me and haven’t played Final Fantasy XIV in a minute, now might be the time to jump back in and finally get through Dawntrail before the new expansion launches in 2027. Starting November 16, players who haven’t logged in to the paid MMORPG in the last five months (150 days specifically) are eligible for 30 days of free playtime.

Players have from November 16th to January 14, 2027 to claim their free 30 days, which means that, if you time it right, your free period will overlap with the launch of the $45 Evercold expansion on February 23. Square Enix has all the specifics here .

The Road to Evercold begins today, helping you prepare for the upcoming release of Evercold!

⭐ 30-day Free Login Campaign ⭐ Tales of Adventure: Winter's Prelude

— FINAL FANTASY XIV (@en.finalfantasyxiv.com) 2026-11-16T10:30:05.686Z

Digging into the details, it seems like Square Enix knows a lot of people (including me) lit out after Endwalker and haven’t been back to play the latest expansion, Dawntrail. In addition to offering free game time, Square Enix is also offering a new $10 Tales of Adventure item which lets players auto-skip main story quest content. It’s designed specifically to leap-frog players over Dawntrail stuff, taking them from the end of Endwalker to the beginning of “In Fate’s Footsteps,” this year’s Evercold -introducing 7.5 event patch.

It is powerfully seductive to pay $10 bucks to take the coward’s way out of Dawntrail . I’ve heard that expansion is just okay, and possibly even worth skipping. But I play Final Fantasy XIV for its story. It can’t always be Heavensward or Shadowbringers , sometimes there has to be a Stormblood in there and that’s okay. As I try to take advantage of the free game time, I’ll finally see Dawntrail for myself.

items.title: Final Fantasy 14 players are gathering in virtual vigils to honour the passing of the game's most prestigious bass player
items.content:
RPG Final Fantasy Final Fantasy 14 Final Fantasy 14 players are gathering in virtual vigils to honour the passing of the game's most prestigious bass player News By Mollie Taylor Published 11 November 2026 The Primals' Eikichi Iwai has died at the age of 57.

(Image credit: Square Enix) {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Facebook X Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 1 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Final Fantasy 14 players have been gathering en masse across servers today in the wake of the news that Eikichi Iwai—the bassist behind the game's band The Primals—has passed away at the age of 57.

A post went out on The Lodestone in the early hours of this morning (November 11) which read: "Thank you very much for your continued support of The Primals. As announced earlier today, we are deeply saddened to share the news of the sudden passing of bassist Eikichi Iwai.

"Having witnessed his truly unforgettable performance on stage at the recent Final Fantasy 14 Fan Festival in Japan, the sudden news of his passing has come as a profound shock. The members of The Primals and the entire FF14 Development and Operations teams are overcome with deep sorrow.

"As we reflect on all that Eikichi-san has left behind, our thoughts are with him, and we offer our heartfelt condolences."

The Primals is Final Fantasy 14's in-house band, fronted by composer Masayoshi Soken and localisation lead Michael-Christopher Koji Fox, and accompanied by Tetsuya Tachibana, GUNN, and Iwai himself.

As Final Fantasy 14's doors remain closed, surviving players are stepping in to keep everyone's crops alive Star Trek Online players are holding public vigils to mourn Patrick Stewart Final Fantasy 14: Evercold delayed to February, preorders start next week FINAL FANTASY XIV: Dark Decades Tour BUDOKAN - Ride the Rhythm Music Video (THE PRIMALS) - YouTube Watch On Iwai's bass in particular has elevated a ton of already-excellent tracks across the game's history: Stormblood's Amatsu Kaze, Shadowbringers' To the Edge, Endwalker's Scream and Close in the Distance, and Dawntrail's Ride the Rhythm just to name a few. The Primals has just come off the back of a strong year for live performances, too—from their usual appearance at all three Fan Festivals that took place this year, to even taking the stage at the UK's biggest rock and music festival as part of Download's lineup .

A quick trip through some of Final Fantasy 14's European servers have seen tons of players gathering in main hubs like Limsa Lominsa to pay their respects and share what it is about Iwai's work that meant so much to them. As I write this story, players and campfires line the perimeter of Omega's Limsa Lominsa plaza—a common practice for honouring the passing of key community figures and beyond, something which I've previously witnessed for the likes of Berserk's creator Kentaro Miura and Dragon Ball creator Akira Toriyama.

By submitting your information you agree to the Terms & Conditions and Privacy Policy and are aged 16 or over. It's a small gesture, but one which is a pleasant reminder of why Final Fantasy 14 continues to maintain such an iron grip on myself and many others.

Mollie Taylor Social Links Navigation Features Producer Mollie spent her early childhood deeply invested in games like Killer Instinct, Toontown and Audition Online, which continue to form the pillars of her personality today. She joined PC Gamer in 2020 as a news writer and now lends her expertise to write a wealth of features, guides and reviews with a dash of chaos. She can often be found causing mischief in Final Fantasy 14, using those experiences to write neat things about her favourite MMO. When she's not staring at her bunny girl she can be found sweating out rhythm games, pretending to be good at fighting games or spending far too much money at her local arcade.

items.title: Fans Gather In Final Fantasy XIV In Memorial For Eikichi Iwai, Bassist For The Primals
items.summary: His passing comes days after he performed at Fan Fest Japan 2026
items.content:
Eikichi Iwai, bassist in the Primals, the official band for Final Fantasy XIV , has passed away. Square Enix and Final Fantasy XIV accounts announced the news of his passing on social media. “We are deeply saddened to share the news of the sudden passing of bassist Eikichi Iwai,” the announcement said . In the wake of Iwai’s passing, memorials are popping up across multiple FFXIV servers as fans remember him and the music he was part of.

In addition to Iwai, the band is led by Final Fantasy FFXIV composer Masayoshi Soken and features musician Gunn on guitar, Tetsuya Tachibana on drums, and Michael-Christopher Koji Fox on vocals. Fans might recognize Koji Fox as being the English localization and translation director for a number of Final Fantasy games.

Much like Nobuo Uematsu’s band the Black Mages, the Primals are known for their rock arrangements and original music for the Final Fanasy XIV soundtrack. W anna hear a rock version of “ Flow “? They got you. You wanna start crying at 10:30 in the morning like I am? “Footfalls” is good for that. I’ll be the first to admit “ To the Edge ” is not one of my favorites out of the Primals’ catalogue (please don’t hurt me), but even I can’t deny Iwai’s sick-ass bass line. His bass makes that song and every one of the Primals’ songs. Iwai’s loss will be profoundly felt.

Square Enix holds Final Fantasy Fan Fests across the world every year featuring a performance by the Primals as one of the main attractions. Iwai’s final performance was at Fan Fest Japan earlier this month, and you can watch a portion of that performance here .

“Going to have The Primals on the whole time I’m playing tonight,” read a comment in the FFXIV subreddit. “Rest easy, Eikichi, thank you for all those basslines.”

items.title: “ZEPHYR” UNVEILED AS SECOND NEW JOB FOR FINAL FANTASY XIV: EVERCOLD, SET TO RELEASE ON TUESDAY 23 rd FEBRUARY 2027
items.summary: Critically Acclaimed MMO Surpasses 35 Million Registered Accounts; Pre-order Information, New EVANGELION Series Crossover Trailer and More Revealed
items.content:
London (31 st October, 2026) – During the FINAL FANTASY XIV Fan Festival 2026 in Tokyo, SQUARE ENIX® announced that its critically acclaimed MMORPG FINAL FANTASY XIV Online has reached more than 35 million registered accounts globally and revealed new information about Evercold , the newest expansion set to release on Tuesday 23 rd February, 2027. During the opening keynote, Producer and Director Naoki Yoshida revealed “zephyr,” the second of two new jobs arriving in Evercold . A physical ranged DPS, zephyr joins the fray using a combination of crossbow shots and support from an avian familiar known as Nephele. A trailer showcasing the zephyr in action can be seen here: https://youtu.be/qX5jtcXjmts The keynote also introduced the full-length trailer for Evercold , which can be seen here: https://youtu.be/4qHEQ2CyOoA

Alongside the release date, Yoshida revealed that pre-orders for the Evercold expansion and the previously announced Collector’s Box will start beginning Wednesday 4 November. 2026 at 9:00 a.m. GMT. The Collector’s Bundle will be available for pre-order in limited quantities exclusively from the Square Enix Store and contains the physical Collector’s Box and a code for the FINAL FANTASY XIV: Evercold Digital Collector’s Edition for Windows® or Mac. PlayStation®5, PlayStation®4, XBOX Series X|S, Nintendo Switch™ 2 and Steam players can order the Collector’s Box as a standalone product and pre-order the Evercold Digital Collector’s Edition separately on their respective platforms. The Evercold Collector’s Box includes the physical goods listed below and does not include a copy of Evercold , in-game items, or pre-order bonuses.

For more information and the latest updates on Evercold , please visit the teaser site at: https://eu.finalfantasyxiv.com/evercold/ The keynote presentation (English language supported) is available to view on YouTube via the Fan Festival 2026 in Tokyo Day 1 live stream: https://www.twitch.tv/videos/2915321914?t=1h32m44s

With more than 35 million total registered accounts, there has never been a better time for newcomers to begin their adventures in the critically acclaimed FINAL FANTASY XIV Online saga. The Free Trial now contains all content from A Realm Reborn , Heavensward , Stormblood and Shadowbringers expansions up through patch 5.58. Free Trial players can enjoy hundreds of hours of award-winning gameplay and story experiences equivalent to four full FINAL FANTASY titles, without limit on playtime. In 2007, the series was relaunched as the Rebuild of EVANGELION film series. Conceived, written and directed by Hideaki Anno, EVANGELION:1.0, 2.0 and 3.0 were all hugely successful, captivating new fans and garnering much praise from a wide range of audiences. The fourth and final film in the series, EVANGELION:3.0+1.0, was released on March 8, 2021, after having been postponed twice due to the COVID-19 pandemic. It recorded 6.73 million admissions, earning 10.2 billion yen at the box office. On March 8, 2023, the long-awaited Blu-ray and DVD, EVANGELION:3.0+1.11 THRICE UPON A TIME was released. October 2025 marked 30 years since the television series debuted, and a celebratory event titled EVANGELION:30+; 30th ANNIVERSARY OF EVANGELION was held in Yokohama Arena between February 21 and 23, 2026. Though such an anniversary event was a first for the series, it proved to be a resounding success, attracting a great many visitors from Japan and around the world. The game is universally regarded as a landmark title of the RPG genre. The original title received high praise for its epic storyline, unique characters, and movie sequences that utilized the most cutting-edge technology of the time. Since then, the game revolving around iconic hero Cloud Strife and his pursuit of the antagonist Sephiroth has sold over 15.7 million copies worldwide and continues to receive widespread acclaim from critics and fans around the world. The popular game has expanded into spin-offs, films and merchandise. Now, Square Enix’s FINAL FANTASY VII Remake Series, created by a team of original and new developers, retells the story of the genre-redefining RPG across three distinct games. The first game of the trilogy, FINAL FANTASY VII REMAKE, is available for PS4® consoles. items.title: Final Fantasy XIV Evercold Delayed, New Release Date Announced at FFXIV Fan Fest
items.summary: The MMORPG's next expansion was set to launch shortly after the new year, but Warriors of Light will have to wait a bit longer.
items.content:
Final Fantasy XIV Evercold was set to launch sometime in January 2027, which was announced as part of its initial reveal back in April this year during the North American FFXIV Fan Fest. However, this next expansion for the critically acclaimed MMORPG has been delayed – FFXIV Evercold's release date is now February 23, 2027 (and February 19, 2027 for early access). This was announced alongside the new, full trailer / intro cinematic for Evercold at FFXIV Fan Fest in Japan, and was said to only be a four-week delay.

In typical FFXIV fashion, the third and final teaser trailer is the full opening cinematic for an expansion, and it kicked off the Japan Fan Fest keynote where director and producer Naoki Yoshida presented more details on new features, where the ongoing story is headed, and fundemental gameplay changes as FFXIV goes into version 8.0 alongside Evercold's launch.

Pre-orders for Evercold open on November 4, 2026 and will come with a Wind-up Kottr minion to summon and follow you around in the world and Halone's Earring which will boost the EXP you gain for Jobs under level 100 when equipped. The collector's edition comes with the Valhallar Odin mount, the Entreat Crystal emote, and the Crystal Skyltborg which looks like glam for the new Bastion Job's weapons. The physical collector's bundle has the Evercold art book, the Tapestry of the Fourth decoration, a Kottr plush, a keychain of the Ethos Metal, and the Warrior of Light Reaper figure.

Additionally, we got a glimpse of the second new Job coming to his new expansion. It's a ranged DPS called Zephyr, which rocks a crossbow as their primary weapon and commands an avian companion to provide support.

There's a lot coming to FFXIV Evercold in addition to a new world and main story including a Neon Genesis Evangelion crossover raid series (which got a new teaser trailer) , a Final Fantasy VII crossover raid series, a new Tank Job with Bastion, and much more. Be sure to check out my Dawntrail review as well to look back at the last expansion before heading into this new era for FFXIV.

Michael is reviews editor at IGN and regularly contributes with previews, interviews, live events coverage, and news all in written and video form. He's usually entrusted with covering long RPGs and tech products, but he's got range when it comes to games. You'll also catch him at conventions and hosting video content, including IGN's weekly podcast Unlocked .

items.content:
Keybound Brawler, a new event that tests your typing prowess, is coming to the Manderville Gold Saucer! The first iteration of the event will be a special collaboration with the FINAL FANTASY VII REMAKE series. Participate in the collaboration stages to obtain MGC which can be exchanged for numerous rewards, including collaboration attire, a mount, emote, and more!

Event Duration

From Wednesday, October 28, 2026 at 1:00 a.m. (PDT) / 8:00 (GMT) / 19:00 (AEDT) to the release of Patch 8.0 * The end date listed on Steam does not reflect the release date for Patch 8.0.

How to Participate

Begin the quest "Keyward Bound" by speaking to the Catlike Mammet in The Gold Saucer (X:5.4 Y:7.0). * Players must be level 15 and above to start the quest. * Players must first complete one of the following main scenario quests: "The Gridanian Envoy," "The Ul'dahn Envoy," or "The Lominsan Envoy." * Players must first complete the quest "It Could Happen to You" to be able to travel to the Manderville Gold Saucer via airship from any of the three city-states. * Please note that a keyboard is required to participate in this content. Gamepads and on-screen keyboards cannot be used.

Rewards

* After this collaboration event has ended, it will be held as a special event at irregular intervals. Visit the special site for more details.

items.title: How a data centre united Australia's gaming community
items.source: ABC News & Headlines – Australian Broadcasting Corporation
items.summary: After years of playing on distant worlds, Australian gamers of the popular Japanese role-playing game Final Fantasy XIV discovered a new home. Now that community has welcomed the game developers Down Under.
items.content:
Michael-Christopher Koji Fox (left) and Toshio Murouchi (right) were the main attractions for players at PAX Australia. ( Supplied: Square Enix )

Link copied Share Share article Before the Oceania data centre arrived, Australians sometimes found the online role-playing game Final Fantasy XIV a surprisingly lonely multiplayer experience.

On the Asia server, they'd struggle to find enough fellow English speakers to tackle the game's notorious super-bosses. Those visiting American servers would find the in-game Golden Saucer amusement park sparsely populated during another time zone's twilight hours.

And the few who chose the most distant Europe server struggled with "input lag" that perilously delayed gameplay actions, with the risk of failed quests and let-down teammates.

That changed in January 2022, 12 years after the game was released, when, encouraged by a pandemic boom in player numbers, developer Square Enix finally launched Oceania servers. It was a decision that united players in the region.

Lin, a Final Fantasy XIV community organiser from Melbourne, was shocked at the scale of the local player base.

"When they finally released a server where our ping [internet connection latency speed] was manageable, we were like, 'whoa, there's thousands of people here'," they tell ABC Arts.

"It took 30 minutes just to get into the queue. You no longer had to guess if we could speak the same language or understand the same lingo."

Final Fantasy's near-40-year legacy lured Pat, another community organiser from Melbourne, into online role-playing games.

"I love the Final Fantasy series. That's the one I grew up with," they say.

The Final Fantasy series has nabbed more than 212 million sales. ( Supplied: Square Enix )

By nature, Final Fantasy XIV's community primarily exists online. A community organisation called Jjammin' runs in-game award shows, theatre shows and musical productions throughout the year.

For many in the region's broader Final Fantasy XIV community, the annual Limsa Extreme meet-up at PAX Australia, one of the country's biggest exhibitions of games and gaming culture, is the highlight on the calendar.

Limsa Extreme was created in 2022 by head organiser Kiya, who was determined to make up for the absence of official events and meetups in Australia. Since then, the event has drawn players from across ANZ, Malaysia and Indonesia, and now even the Japan-based developers.
